correctness.rationale: For each q>=2, an adjacency-distinct palindrome has unique form v c reverse(v) with c distinct from v final symbol. The palindrome midpoint lemma (Barker et al. Proposition 15, previously known) gives index 2a or 2a+1 according as the final incomplete arch plus c completes the full alphabet. The generating functions B_{q,s} count levels of the discovered-letter automaton with s-1 old-letter choices and q-s new-letter choices; arch weight alpha_q z^q/D_q with alpha_q=(q-1)(q-1)!. The centered correction multiplies exactly the q-1-letter residual by (u-1); checking initial vs subsequent arch weights yields F_q=q[1+(q-1)sum_s B_{q,s}+(u-1)B_{q,q-1}]/(1-u^2 alpha_q z^q/D_q). Exact minimal lengths follow by making every full arch a permutation and the terminal deficient remainder distinct-letter. q=2, empty halves, h=0, zero index and q-1 symbol residual all addressed. Finite brute coefficient checks independently match.
residual_risks: Finite independent computations corroborate but do not prove the arbitrary-parameter theorem unless the stated finite universe was exhaustively enumerated.
